title: chant workspace exit output
description: What `chant workspace exit [<member>...] --json` prints (#3177): the drill report with --drill, and otherwise the staged exit, its drill report and the outcome of the gate. A refused member carries one of the codes in $defs.memberResult.properties.code, and a drill finding one of the codes in $defs.finding.properties.code; both are in the one closed list of `reason-codes.ts`. A failure that stops the command before it prints this document (no such member, a dirty tree, no git repository) prints an error message and exits 1. Readers ignore fields they do not know; a field is only ever added within a version.

drill.description: --drill: the exit run on a scratch copy and checked. Exit code 0 when ok, else 1.

ok.description: True when no member failed. A not-run member does not fail the drill.

exit.description: The exit staged in a worktree. Exit code 0 for nothing-to-exit, dry-run and applied, 1 for checks-failed and 3 for gated.

digest.description: sha256: and the first 16 hex digits of the staged patch. The gate binds it.

pending.description: With outcome gated: the pending gate fact, as the gate ledger records it.

approvedBy.description: With outcome applied: who approved the gate.

report.description: The drill's checks of the staged tree.

memberResult.description: What the exit did to one member.

code.description: With status refused: why the member can't be exited.

native.description: Native files written, relative to the workspace root.

deploy.description: The stock command for each native file, relative to the member's directory.

ci.description: CI files rewritten or written, relative to the workspace root.

ops.description: op.json files left in place, relative to the workspace root.

steps.description: Steps a person runs, for a member the exit can't do alone.

drillMember.description: The drill's verdict on one member.

note.description: Why the member is not-run or kept.

finding.description: One thing the drill found wrong with an exited member.
